title: Real Estate in a Pandemic: Homeowners and Buyers (Part 1)

reader_summary.headline: Hi and welcome to the A16D podcast.
reader_summary.overview: Hi and welcome to the A16D podcast. This episode is the first in a two-part series that examines the pandemic's impact on real estate. Part one focuses on prospective homebuyers, sellers, and existing homeowners. Part two addresses renters and landlords.

key_points.text: How has social distancing shaken up the market to buy?
key_points.evidence_quote: How has social distancing shaken up the market to buy?

key_points.text: What's the ripple effect of eviction freezes and a record number of homes and forbearance?
key_points.evidence_quote: What's the ripple effect of eviction freezes and a record number of homes and forbearance?

key_points.text: And how can tech streamline the inefficient process of renting, buying, or selling a home?

key_points.text: This episode features A16C general partner Alex Rompel, who's invested in a number of real estate companies.

thesis: The episode examines the pandemic's impact on real estate, noting a historic drop in home supply due to sellers waiting out the crisis and buyer nervousness. It argues that the ability to work from home is shifting supply and demand curves by allowing high-income workers to move from expensive areas like the San Francisco Bay Area to cheaper locations, which could significantly alter home prices and market dynamics.
